items.label: section_header
items.text: HINT

items.label: text
items.text: Not looking carefully at word endings is one of the most common mistakes students make when they start to write formulae. Be careful!

items.label: section_header
items.text: KEYPOINT

items.label: text
items.text: If you didn't write the brackets, the formula would look like this: BaNO32. That would read as 1 barium, 1 nitrogen and 32 oxygens!

items.label: section_header
items.text: CONFUSING ENDINGS!

items.label: text
items.text: Don't confuse ions such as sulfate and sulfide. A name like copper(Il) sulfide means that it contains copper and sulfur only. Any ide' ending means that there isn't anything complicated there. Sodium chloride, for example, is just sodium and chlorine combined together. So copper(ll) sulfide contains Cu²+ and S²- ions.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Figure 7.11 Copper(II) sulfide is CuS.

items.label: text
items.text: Once you have an 'ate' ending, it means that there is oxygen (and possibly other things) there as well. So, for example, copper(Il) sulfate contains copper, sulfur and oxygen.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Figure 7.12 Copper(II)sulfate isCuSO4.

items.label: section_header
items.text: DEDUCING THE FORMULA FOR AN IONIC COMPOUND

items.label: section_header
items.text: EXAMPLE1

items.label: section_header
items.text: To find the formula for sodium oxide

items.label: text
items.text: Sodium is in Group 1, so the ion is Na+.

items.label: text
items.text: Oxygen is in Group 6, so the ion is O²-.

items.label: text
items.text: To have equal numbers of positive and negative charges, you would need two sodium ions to provide the two positive charges to cancel the two negative charges on one oxide ion. In other words, you need:

items.label: text
items.text: Na+

items.label: text
items.text: Na+

items.label: text
items.text: The formula is therefore NaO.

items.label: section_header
items.text: EXAMPLE 2

items.label: section_header
items.text: To find the formula for barium nitrate

items.label: text
items.text: Barium is in Group 2, so the ion is Ba²+.

items.label: text
items.text: Nitrate ions are NO3-. You will have to remember this.

items.label: text
items.text: To have equal numbers of positive and negative charges, you would need two nitrate ions for each barium ion.

items.label: text
items.text: The formula is Ba(NO₃)2.

items.label: text
items.text: Notice the brackets around the nitrate group. Brackets must be written if you have more than one of these complex ions (ions containing more than one atom). In any other situation, they are completely unnecessary.
